transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess I came in because I can’t shake this feeling that people are sort of… watching how I move professionally. Like, certain people in the arts and finance circles around Cincinnati, they seem to know which clients I’m meeting with, or they send little signals—through invitations, or the topics on panels, or even who ends up sitting near me at events.

I know that probably sounds strange. And I tell myself, you know, maybe it’s just coincidence. Cincinnati’s smaller than people think—everybody knows everybody, especially if you go to enough fundraisers and networking things—but I just can’t really let it go. It keeps feeling intentional.
Do you think it’s possible that this feeling is mistaken, or are you certain those people are intentionally sending you signals?

I mean… I know it could be mistaken, technically. I do tell myself that. Like, Cincinnati isn’t that big, and if you’re around the arts boards and finance people enough, you run into the same names, the same clients, the same gala committees.

But then something happens—like an invitation comes right after I meet with a certain client, or a panel topic feels too specific, or someone gets seated near me who… just shouldn’t be there by chance—and I’m back to thinking, no, this is intentional. I can’t really let it go. It feels like they’re quietly tracking me and sending these little signals.
Have you had the feeling that your thoughts are being controlled or interfered with by someone else?

Controlled? I don’t… I don’t think I’d put it that way. Like, nobody’s steering my thoughts like a remote control or anything.

Sometimes I’ll get stuck on something, like a phrase from a meeting or the way someone said something at an event, and it’ll loop in my head longer than I want. But that happens to people, right? Especially in my work, because if you miss one little detail with a client it can turn into a whole issue later. So… I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by interfered with. I haven’t really noticed someone else getting into my thoughts, no.
Do these thoughts about people sending you signals feel intrusive and unwanted, like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Yeah… I mean, sort of. They don’t feel like random thoughts exactly, not like something silly popping in. It’s more like once something happens — like an invitation shows up after I’ve met with a client, or a panel topic lines up a little too neatly — I can’t stop turning it over.

And I know, I know, people would say that’s just coincidence, especially here, because the arts people and the finance people overlap way more than you’d think. I was at this one event where the seating chart alone felt like someone was making a point, but then again those committees all talk to each other, so maybe—

But, yes, I guess they’re unwanted in the sense that I don’t want to spend my day thinking about it. I just can’t really let it go when it feels like certain people are quietly tracking who I’m meeting with and sending signals around it.
When these thoughts come up, do they feel to you like a real warning about what people are doing, or more like a thought your mind gets stuck on even though you suspect it may not be true?

It feels like a warning at the time. That’s the hard part. I can tell myself afterward, okay, maybe this is just Cincinnati being small, people from the arts boards and the finance side all mixing together, same events, same donor lists—honestly those circles overlap in weird ways.

But when it happens, like an invitation shows up right after I’ve met with someone, or a panel topic sounds a little too close to something I was dealing with, or I get seated near somebody who connects back to a client… it doesn’t feel like just a thought I’m stuck on. It feels like they’re doing it on purpose, like they’re signaling that they know who I’m meeting with.

And then later I’ll go back and forth with myself, but I can’t really shake it.
Have you heard or seen things that other people could not?

I don’t think so. I mean, not like seeing a person standing there that nobody else sees, or hearing a voice talking to me when the room is quiet.

Sometimes at events, there’s so much noise—people talking over each other, music, the clinking glasses, you know—and I’ll think I heard my name or something about a client, but then it’s usually just… noise, or I can’t tell. That happens in crowded rooms. Those fundraisers are terrible for that, honestly, the acoustics are always bad.

But if you mean clear things other people couldn’t hear or see, no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump between ideas in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?

I’m not sure. I mean, not usually? People sometimes tell me I’m giving too much background, but that’s different, I think. Like with work, if I’m explaining a portfolio decision, I want to explain the context, because if you don’t understand the market setup then the recommendation sounds random.

My sister has said I “circle around the point,” which—yeah, maybe. But I don’t think people say I don’t make sense. I think they just get impatient before I’ve laid out why something connects. Some people want the headline first, and I’m more… I guess I build up to it.

So, hard to follow? Maybe occasionally, if I’m stressed or trying to explain too many pieces at once. But I haven’t really had people say I’m jumping between ideas in a way that makes no sense.
How long have you been having this feeling that people are intentionally tracking you and sending you signals?

It’s been… about two months, I think. Maybe a little more depending on where I start counting it, because at first it was just one or two odd coincidences and I didn’t really label it that way.

But the feeling that people are actually tracking my client meetings and sending little signals about it—that’s been around for roughly two months. It’s kind of grown in my mind since then.
Right now, do you believe these people really are intentionally tracking you and sending you signals?

Right now… yes, I think I do. I mean, I can tell you there’s a part of me that says, okay, maybe invitations get worded strangely, maybe a panel topic lines up with something I just discussed with a client because finance people all talk about the same few things, and Cincinnati is smaller than people think—especially the arts boards and the donor circles and all that.

But then it keeps happening. Like who gets seated near me at an event, or some little comment in an invitation, or the topic of a panel right after I’ve had a meeting, and it feels too specific to just shrug off. That’s actually why I came in, because I can’t really let it go.

So… I don’t know if “know” is the right word, but yes, I do believe certain people are tracking who I’m meeting with and sending signals about it. Even when I try to talk myself out of it, it still feels real.
Since this started, have there been any days when the belief that people are tracking you and sending signals went away completely?

Not really completely, no. I mean, some days it’s quieter, if I’m busy with actual client work or I’m not going to events or looking at invitations. But it doesn’t fully go away.

It’s like… I can tell myself, “Okay, maybe that panel topic was already planned,” or “maybe the seating thing is just random,” because these arts and finance circles in Cincinnati overlap more than people realize. But then I’ll see something—an invitation wording, who ends up near me, something that lines up with a meeting I had—and it comes back.

So I wouldn’t say there have been days where I’m totally free of it. Maybe moments where I can push it aside, but not gone.
Has this belief been present for longer than three months?

No, not longer than three months. I’d put it at about two months… maybe a little around the edges, because I keep thinking back to when I first noticed things, like invitations or who was seated where, but the actual belief that my client meetings were being tracked and people were sending signals about it—about two months.
Since this started, have there been times when you felt very confused or puzzled about what was happening around you?

Yeah… puzzled, definitely. Confused is maybe the right word, but not like I don’t know where I am or anything. More like I keep trying to figure out what’s actually happening.

I’ll get an invitation or see a panel topic, or notice who’s sitting near me at one of these events, and it lines up with clients I’ve met with, and then I’m stuck going over it. And Cincinnati has all these overlapping arts and finance circles—my friend on one board knows someone at a foundation, someone else’s spouse works in wealth management, it’s all connected—so part of me says, “Of course people know things.”

But then another part is like, why would that exact topic come up right after that meeting? Why that wording? Why that person near me? So yes, I’ve felt pretty puzzled by it. That’s kind of why I came in, because I can’t sort it out or just let it go.
Since this started, have the people close to you noticed a big change in how you’ve been acting day to day?

Yeah… a little, I think. Not like I’m falling apart or anything. I still get work done, just kind of in chunks, and sometimes I’ll leave client follow-ups sitting longer than I should.

My friends have noticed I’m not showing up as much. Like I used to go to jazz nights, and there’s pickup basketball too, and lately I just… don’t go. Which is weird because I used to have opinions about who was playing sax at Schwartz’s or whether the court at the park was too crowded, and now I don’t really care enough to argue about it.

When people ask what’s going on, I give short answers. It just feels like a lot of effort to explain anything. So, yeah, I guess people close to me have noticed I’m more flat or less interested day to day.
Have you heard voices speaking to you when no one else was there?

I don’t think so… not like an actual voice talking to me in an empty room.

Sometimes I’ll replay conversations in my head after a client meeting, or think I heard someone say something at an event and then I’m not sure because there’s music or people talking over each other—like those gallery openings where everyone’s pretending to look at one painting but really they’re networking. But voices speaking to me when no one’s there… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Did this sense that people were tracking you come on suddenly over a few days?

No, not over just a few days. I mean… there were probably little things before I really admitted I was noticing them, if that makes sense.

But the actual feeling that people were tracking my client meetings and then sort of sending signals back to me through events or wording or who showed up nearby—that’s been going on maybe two months. It’s hard to pin down because I keep thinking of earlier examples, like, “Was that part of it too?” But around two months is when it really became a thing I couldn’t ignore.
Since this started, have you felt emotionally flat or like your feelings have been noticeably reduced?

Yeah… I mean, “flat” sounds kind of dramatic, but maybe that’s right.

I still do things, like work doesn’t just stop—I’ll get through client stuff in pieces, a few calls here, some paperwork later. But there’s not the same spark to it. I’ll leave follow-ups sitting longer than I should, and then I’ll look at them like… why is this so hard, it’s just an email.

And outside work, yeah, I’ve been skipping jazz nights and pickup basketball. I used to care about that stuff. I’d have opinions about the music, or who was playing rough on the court, or whatever. Now it’s more like… I could go, but I don’t feel much pull.

When friends ask me what’s going on, I usually just give short answers. Not because I’m trying to be rude. Talking just feels like more effort than it should.
Have you had the feeling that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know what you were thinking?

Not exactly like people can hear the sentence in my head, no. It’s more… I’ve had this feeling that certain people around the arts events and some finance people here in Cincinnati seem to know what I’ve been doing—like which clients I’ve met with—and then it shows up in these little ways.

Like an invitation comes through with wording that feels too close, or a panel topic lines up strangely, or someone ends up sitting near me who really shouldn’t have a reason to be there. And I know, okay, maybe that sounds like coincidence, and Cincinnati is smaller than people think—everyone overlaps, especially those fundraiser-type events—but I can’t really shake it once I notice it. It feels like signals. Not my thoughts being broadcast exactly, but like they’re tracking me somehow.
Have you felt that someone was putting thoughts into your mind that were not your own?

I don’t think so… not like a thought just appears and I’m like, “That’s not mine.” I mean, sometimes I’ll second-guess why I’m thinking about something, especially if it connects to something that just happened, but that’s different, right?

Like with work, I’ll be trying to focus on a client spreadsheet and then suddenly remember some random conversation from a fundraiser or something, and I’ll wonder why that came up—but I wouldn’t say someone put it there. My mind jumps around anyway, especially when I’m stressed.

So… no, I haven’t really felt like thoughts were being inserted into my head.
Have you felt that outside forces were controlling your actions or movements?

No, I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve never felt like my arms or legs were being moved by someone else, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes I’ll get stuck and not do something I meant to do, like I’ll sit there longer than I should before making a call or getting out the door, but that feels more like me hesitating or getting distracted. Not like a force is controlling my body.

Unless you mean something more subtle? I don’t know. I haven’t noticed anything like being physically controlled.
Since this started, have there been times when you became unable to move or speak for a while, even though you were awake?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had moments where I kind of freeze up socially, like if I’m at one of those networking things and there’s too many people around, I’ll pause and not know what to say for a second… but I can still move, I can still talk if I force it.

Not like being awake and unable to speak or move for a while. I don’t think I’ve had that.

But then I’ll see something—an invitation wording, who ends up near me, something that lines up with a meeting I had—and it comes back.

So I wouldn’t say there have been days where I’m totally free of it. Maybe moments where I can push it aside, but not gone.

But then another part is like, why would that exact topic come up right after that meeting? Why that wording? Why that person near me? So yes, I’ve felt pretty puzzled by it. That’s kind of why I came in, because I can’t sort it out or just let it go.
